citation.title: Benchmarking LLMs in Political Content Text-Annotation: Proof-of-Concept with Toxicity and Incivility Data
citation.venue_or_publisher: arXiv preprint (cs.CL), prepared for the 8th Monash-Warwick-Zurich Text-as-Data Workshop, 16-17 September 2024

question: How well do Google's Perspective API, OpenAI GPT models and locally deployed open-source LLMs perform zero-shot annotation of toxicity in political social media content, measured against a human-coded gold standard, and how do they compare on speed and reproducibility (including under different temperature settings)?
data: More than 3.5 million Twitter/X messages about protest events: Argentina (n = 551,761; August 2020) and Chile (n = 3,125,254; October 2019), collected by hashtags that exceeded 50,000 posts. Gold standard: balanced random sample of 1,000 messages (500 per country), stratified by Perspective toxicity quintiles, each hand-coded by two of five human coders in Labelbox (7.2 hours of annotation, 1.2 hours of revision). Brazilian (Portuguese) messages were excluded.
method: Binary toxicity labelling (TOXIC / NONTOXIC). Perspective API run on the full corpus (thresholds 0.55 and 0.70). Zero-shot classification with 5 GPT models and 10 open-source LLMs (deployed locally with Ollama at minimum temperature), using the human coders' instruction as the system message plus a restricted-output instruction. Compared with accuracy, precision, recall, F1, Jaccard distance, computing time. A preliminary benchmark (pre-PoC, in the Appendix) used Perspective scores as proxy labels with tenfold cross-validation to select models. Temperature experiments (minimum, 0.25, 1.00, same seed) assessed with bootstrapped Krippendorff's alpha (1,000 iterations).

definitions.definition: Rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable comments likely to make someone leave the discussion or stop sharing their perspective; taken from the core definitions of Perspective.
definitions.quote: TOXIC: Rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable comments that are likely to make someone leave the discussion or stop sharing their perspective.

definitions.definition: Civil or nice comments unlikely to discourage conversation.
definitions.quote: NONTOXIC: Civil or nice comments that are unlikely to discourage conversation

definitions.definition: Open-source models with seven or fewer billion parameters.
definitions.quote: some open-source so-called Small Language Models (SLMs), which have seven or fewer billion parameters

definitions.definition: No single definition adopted; the paper notes the literature uses a variety of conceptualisations (vulgarity, profanity, identity-based attacks, hate speech). Incivility is not separately defined or coded in this paper despite the title.
definitions.quote: there are a variety of conceptualisations that could include vulgarity, profanity, identity-based attacks, and hate speech, among others

proxies.indicator: Binary label from two human coders per message, using the Perspective-derived TOXIC/NONTOXIC definition
proxies.quote: Each message was hand-coded by two different coders of the team, therefore, we have two ground-truth labels for each sample observation.

proxies.indicator: Perspective API score (predicted probability) with a cut-off; 0.55 ('laxer') and 0.70 ('standard') thresholds compared
proxies.quote: we used Perspective score with a laxer threshold of 0.55 and a standard of 0.70

proxies.indicator: Perspective score used in place of human labels in the pre-PoC benchmark for model selection
proxies.quote: we ran a preliminary benchmark using Perspective API as a proxy of ground-truth labels instead of the gold standard elaborated by human annotators

proxies.indicator: Lower bound of bootstrapped Krippendorff's alpha 95% CI above 0.80 across re-runs and temperature settings
proxies.quote: test if the lower confidence interval is above the 0.80 threshold considered reliable

findings.claim: Perspective API with the laxer 0.55 threshold had the highest F1 against the human gold standard, outperforming all GPTs and open-source LLMs; the same model at 0.70 ranked last (F1 about 0.70).
findings.quote: Perspective API, Google's model distilled from BERT family models, with a laxer cut-off threshold of Perspective score at 0.55, outperforms the GPTs and open-source LLMs we have tested

findings.claim: GPT-4o and Nous Hermes 2 Mixtral (47B) were the best LLM zero-shot classifiers, with F1 around 0.84 and 0.835 (Table 1); GPT-3.5 Turbo was lowest (F1 0.762). All models exceeded F1 0.70.
findings.quote: all the models tested showed F1-scores above 0.70, even some outdated versions such as GPT-3.5 Turbo

findings.claim: Most GPTs and several open models had high recall but lower precision (over-predicting toxic); Table 1 shows recall of 0.95-0.99 with precision of 0.62-0.74 for many models. [from a table on this page; no quotable sentence]

Small locally deployed models (Nous Hermes 2, Mistral OpenOrca) reached good performance at about 2.35 seconds per message; larger parameter count was associated with higher performance, computing time was not.
findings.quote: the number of billions of parameters is significant (p = 0.003)

findings.claim: Speed: GPTs were fastest (0.511 to 0.852 s per observation); open-source LLMs about 6x faster than human coders (average human time 15.125 s per message), Perspective about 13x, GPTs about 24x.
findings.quote: open-source LLMs are almost 6x faster than human coders

findings.claim: GPTs could not guarantee full reproducibility even with fixed seed, though reliability was relatively high; GPT-4 showed marked fluctuation across temperature levels. Open-source models run locally at minimum temperature were fully reproducible.
findings.quote: only through open-source models deployed locally at a minimum level of temperature is possible to ensure reproducibility in the annotation output

findings.claim: Human coders agreed very strongly on the gold standard.
findings.quote: The inter-coder reliability was excellent: Cohen's κ 0.944

findings.claim: Model clusters in Jaccard distance: a high-performance group (GPT-4o, Aya, GPT-4, Gemma 2 27B, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4 Turbo) and a lower-performance group (Llama 3.1, Gemma 2 9B, Mistral NeMo); some models were dissimilar to others, suggesting scope for ensembles.
findings.quote: which could open avenues for ensemble annotations and the use of stacking classifiers

recommendations.claim: Treat Perspective scores as a probability measure that is too stringent at the standard threshold; use a laxer threshold and consider thresholds carefully when classifying messages.
recommendations.quote: the Perspective score as a probability measure tends to be too stringent and should be considered carefully when classifying messages.

recommendations.claim: GPT-4 should not be used for this kind of annotation because of its instability across temperature settings.
recommendations.quote: except for the case of GPT-4, which suggests that this model should not be used for this type of task

recommendations.claim: Small models deployed locally are a low-cost, reproducible option for classification.
recommendations.quote: This confirms the possibilities that some small models deployed locally with low costs for classification tasks could offer.

recommendations.claim: Future work could add context and prompt variation to improve performance, and try few-shot or chain-of-thought approaches.
recommendations.quote: a potential avenue is incorporating additional context information and prompt variation in the pipeline to improve the classification's performance

limitations.point: Only zero-shot classification with a single short prompt was tested; few-shot, chain-of-thought and prompt variation were not explored.
limitations.quote: exploring some applications beyond zero-shot classification, such as classification tasks involving few-shot ontologies or chain-of-thought, is possible

limitations.point: Larger open-source models (Llama 3.1 70B/405B, Hermes 3 70B/405B and others) could not be run on the authors' hardware, so the open-source comparison is of smaller versions.
limitations.quote: are beyond of our infrastructure's RAM possibilities

limitations.point: OpenAI o1-preview and o1-mini were not tested because they were not yet fully available through the API.
limitations.quote: since they are not fully available to all API users at the moment of writing this paper

limitations.point: Gold standard covers one task (binary toxicity), one platform (Twitter/X), Spanish-language protest messages from two countries, and 1,000 messages; results may not transfer to other classification tasks such as organisation classification. Not stated as a limitation by the authors.

The gold-standard sample was stratified using Perspective score quintiles, so the evaluation set is not drawn independently of one of the compared classifiers (possible bias in Perspective's favour). Not stated as a limitation by the authors.
limitations.quote: Therefore, we balanced the sample by splitting it by country, considering 500 messages from Argentina and 500 from Chile, and then used quintiles of toxicity

limitations.point: Single run per configuration for main benchmark; no confidence intervals on Table 1 metrics; pre-print not peer reviewed. The title mentions incivility but only toxicity is annotated.
Dependence on proprietary models is acknowledged as a risk to reproducibility and openness.
limitations.quote: concerns about dependency on property models owned by for-profit companies, which could jeopardise the reproducibility and openness of research
